title: Little evolution of dust emissivity in bright infrared galaxies from 2 < z < 6
question: Whether the dust emissivity index (\beta) and dust temperature (T_{dust}) in dusty star-forming galaxies evolve with redshift over 2 < z < 6, and whether observed variations and correlations are intrinsic or caused by measurement errors.

data.bands: Band 3 (3 mm), Band 4 (2 mm), Band 6 (1.1-1.4 mm)

what.value: HerBS catalogue and 250, 350, 500, and 850 um photometry

evidence.quote: In our study we have used all HerBS sources with spectroscopic redshifts and photometry at 250, 350 and 500 \mu m (Herschel-SPIRE), at 850 \mu m (Bakx et al. 2018) and at 2 and 3 mm from ALMA (Bendo et al. 2023.

what.value: Spectroscopic redshifts and lensing magnifications for HerBS sources

evidence.quote: In total, Urquhart et al. (2022) measured 71 spectroscopic redshifts for 62 entries in the HerBS catalogue.

To estimate the mass and luminosity of the dust we require an estimate of the lensing magnifications, which we have taken to be those quoted in the lens modelling of Spilker et al. (2016) for the SPT sources and from the correlation between CO luminosity and line width as determined by Urquhart et al. (2022) for HerBS, building on the work of Harris et al. (2012).

recipe.goal: Compile sample and filter by photometric coverage
recipe.method: Select HerBS and SPT DSFGs with spectroscopic redshifts and restrict to sources having at least two photometric measurements at observed wavelengths beyond 1 mm; combine ALMA multiple components within Herschel beams if \Delta z < 0.1.
key_parameters: Minimum 2 photometric points at \lambda_{obs} > 1 mm; \Delta z < 0.1 for multiples
assumptions: Multiple ALMA sources within the Herschel beam with only one spectroscopic redshift are physically connected at that redshift.

recipe.goal: Fit FIR-to-mm SEDs with CMB-adjusted modified blackbody models
recipe.method: Fit a single modified blackbody combined with a mid-IR power-law (corrected for CMB heating and background contrast) using MCMC under four opacity cases: optically thin, \lambda_1 = 100 \mu m, \lambda_1 = 200 \mu m, and fixed physical area (for 37 SPT sources).
key_parameters: Free parameters: M_{dust}, T_{dust}, \beta, \alpha (and \nu_1 in general opacity models); L_{IR} integrated over rest-frame 8-1000 \mu m
assumptions: \Lambda CDM cosmology with H_0 = 67.7 km s^-1 Mpc^-1 and \Omega_m = 0.31
\kappa_0 = 0.077 m^2 kg^-1 at \nu_0 = 353 GHz; T_{CMB,0} = 2.73 K; \mu = 1 when unlensed

recipe.goal: Quantify correlation between beta and dust temperature
recipe.method: Calculate Pearson (r_{Pearson}) and Spearman rank (\rho_{Spearman}) correlation coefficients between \beta and T_{dust} for the optically-thin model fits.

recipe.goal: Simulate mock SEDs to assess parameter recovery, correlated errors, and intrinsic scatter in beta
recipe.method: Generate mock SEDs from the optically-thin model with parameters drawn from uniform distributions, add normal observational errors, apply survey flux detection limits (>80 mJy at 500 \mu m for HerBS; >25 mJy at 870 \mu m for SPT), and refit with the same SED fitting routine.
key_parameters: Flat bounds: log(\mu L_{IR}) = 13-14 (HerBS) and 13-14.5 (SPT), T_{dust} = 20-50 K, \beta = 0.5-4 (or 1\sigma range 1.68-2.41 for SPT and 1.61-2.26 for HerBS in Section 5.2), \alpha = 1-5; z = 2-4 (HerBS) and 2-6 (SPT)
assumptions: Lensing magnification \mu = 5.5 for mock SPT galaxies and \mu = 5.3 for mock HerBS galaxies

recipe.goal: Test whether interferometric flux loss at 3 mm explains extreme beta values
recipe.method: Repeat SED fitting without the 3-mm ALMA photometry and with fixed \beta = 2 for five extreme-\beta SPT sources, comparing predicted and observed 3-mm flux densities.

recipe.goal: Measure evolution of dust temperature with redshift at fixed IR luminosity
recipe.method: Select a luminosity-limited subset of galaxies, calculate peak dust temperature T_{peak} from \lambda_{peak} using Wien's displacement law, and perform bootstrap fitting of a linear model of T_{peak} versus redshift.
key_parameters: T_{peak} = 2.898 x 10^3 [\mu m K] / \lambda_{peak} [\mu m]; detection limits calculated with T_{dust} = 32 K and \beta = 2
assumptions: Wien's displacement law relates \lambda_{peak} to T_{peak} independent of dust opacity model.

answer_key.quantity: Median dust emissivity index \beta (combined sample, optically thin)

evidence.quote: We find no evidence of a change in \beta with redshift, with a median value of \beta = 1.96 for the optically-thin model with a confidence interval (16–84%) of 1.67 to 2.35 for the population.

answer_key.quantity: Pearson correlation coefficient r_{Pearson} between \beta and T_{dust} (SPT)

evidence.quote: The values (r_{Pearson} = -0.83 and \rho_{Spearman} = -0.87 for SPT; r_{Pearson} = -0.89 and \rho_{Spearman} = -0.89 for HerBS) show that the SPT and HerBS galaxies exhibit a strong negative \beta–T_{dust} correlation and the similarity between the two metrics suggests that few galaxies deviate from the trend.
